rationale: This is a near-cosmetic variant of the archived "Maturity-Wall Gross Profit Trend" (same IND_ADJ gross-profit trend × dlc/lt × lt/at core) with only a 3-observation VOL penalty bolted on — a construction that already backfired in "Debt-Pressure Profit Durability" — and subtracting a noisy 3-period standard deviation from a 3-period slope is statistically fragile rather than economically substantive.

The core driver, ΔLT/AT, is close to the well-known net-financing/leverage-change anomaly and the "self-funded deleveraging" idea was already tested weakly in this archive, but conditioning paydown jointly on gross-profit trend and near-term maturity share is a defensible reordering (paydown as the base signal rather than the modifier) that is worth one test.

It uses exactly the same three rank components as the archived "Net-Current-Debt Cost Stickiness," so it is close to a variant, but swapping the skewed triple-product for a MIN intersection is a legitimate, explicitly diagnosed response to that signal's strong alpha (t=-5.0) coexisting with a near-zero and wrong-signed FMB slope.

This is the archived "Maturity-Wall Cash-Backed Profit Quality" with the conditioner changed from RANK(dlc/lt) to SUMRANK(dlc/lt, NEG(che/at)) — a single-leg addition already used in two other archived signals — which is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new mechanism.

Gross profit scaled by SG&A plus depreciation is a genuinely new denominator in this archive (an operating-leverage coverage measure rather than another asset-scaled profitability), though it flirts with the known operating-leverage anomaly and the (lct−act)/at conditioner has produced consistently weak results in prior generations, and small overhead denominators will make the ratio heavy-tailed despite winsorization.

ΔRE/AT is essentially net income less dividends over assets, so the "equity cushion rebuild" framing is largely a relabeled profitability signal, and multiplying it by RANK(oibdp/at) double-counts the same profitability information rather than supplying an independent conditioning state.
